label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: support@clockpoint.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: kevin.mutua@tausifreight.example
Subject: Re: [CP-48213] Overtime coding issue on night shifts

Dear Faith,

Thank you for picking this up. Here are the details you asked for.

1. Terminals and firmware: four BX-300 terminals at our Embakasi depot, now on firmware 4.2.1. They auto-updated from 4.1.8 on the night of 27 October. Our two BX-300s at Mombasa Road were offline that week, are still on 4.1.8 and are not affected.

2. Shift template: NIGHT-8 (22:00 to 06:00).

3. Example: employee ID T-0417 clocked in at 21:54 on 30 October and out at 06:07 on 31 October.
Export showed: 2.1 hrs REG on 30 October and 6.1 hrs OT15 on 31 October.
Expected: 8.0 hrs REG plus 0.2 hrs OT15. We round to the nearest tenth of an hour, so the 8 h 13 min total is 8.2 hrs, with only the 13 minutes outside the scheduled shift coded OT15.

4. Export profile: Payroll CSV v2.

5. First noticed: 5 November, during the review of our draft October overtime. The affected records start from about 28 October, the day after the firmware update.

In short, any shift that crosses midnight is being split into two lines, and the after-midnight line is coded OT15 instead of REG. All 38 staff on the Embakasi night shift are affected. The 4.2.1 release notes promised improved midnight rollover handling for shifts spanning two calendar days, and it has done the exact opposite for us.

One direct question: can our IT officer, Brian Ochieng, safely roll the four Embakasi terminals back to 4.1.8 without losing any punch data? He is able to do it but will not proceed until you confirm it is safe. If there are steps he should take first, kindly spell them out.

Our November payroll inputs close on Friday 20 November, so we need either a fix or a clear workaround before that date. We corrected October manually from the raw punches and cannot do that every month.

I have copied Kevin Mutua, our payroll officer. He will test whatever you suggest and can send further examples if you need them.

Kind regards,
Njeri Mwangi
HR Manager, Tausi Freight
